title: Grammatici Latini Vol. VI Pt. 1: Scriptores Artis Metricae
shelf_note: Keil's 1857 Teubner edition of the Latin metricians (this page: Marius Victorinus). It fits a Toronto/PIMS collection of Latin grammatical texts.
structure_note: This record is page 148 and the printed page is 142, a steady offset of 6 for front matter. The 3 backsteps and 3 repeats are probably misread numerals or plates; nothing on this page points to a splice. The counts disagree on translations: structure.pages_translated is 0, but pages_translated_field is 294, so one of the counters is stale.

pages.layout: single column; verse quotations indented and spaced; line numbers 5–30 in the outer margin; two footnote blocks below a rule (loci paralleli, then critical apparatus)

ocr_errors.problem: e-caudata normalised to plain e in the apparatus. This is a manuscript reading, so the spelling counts as data.

ocr_errors.image: footnote apparatus below a rule at the foot of the page
ocr_errors.problem: Both footnote blocks (parallels and critical apparatus) are tagged <margin> instead of as notes or apparatus

tr_errors.source: 8 suprema detracta ς supremo detracta *B Val.*
tr_errors.english: Line 8, "suprema detracta" is the reading of the later manuscripts <note>siglum ς</note>; "supremo detracta" B and Valerius
tr_errors.problem: The translator expands the sigla. The page does not say that ς means 'later manuscripts', and in Keil it usually marks the old editions. 'Val.' is expanded to a person, 'Valerius', but it is more likely a witness siglum (a manuscript or edition). Both expansions are unsupported and misdescribe the apparatus. The Latin body text is not affected.

other.note: Centering arrows '->…<-' around the verse quotations, carried from the OCR into the translation (e.g. '->"Damoetas and Lyctian Aegon."<-'). They are raw markup if the renderer does not convert them.
The summary names Archilochus as the subject ('how Archilochus derived new meters'), but no name appears on this page. The subject of 'edidit/protulit' comes from an earlier page.
The OCR <meta> line 'p. 2589. 90 P. p. 194. 95 G.' (concordance with the Putsch and Gaisford editions) appears as a <margin> in the translation, with no explanation

missing.why: The witness sigla A, B and ς are never explained. The reader cannot tell manuscripts from editions, and the inline expansion 'later manuscripts' is unsupported.
'Val.' is a siglum (a witness), not a scholar named Valerius. The reader needs to know what it denotes.

This is a concordance to the pages of the Putsch (P.) and Gaisford (G.) editions. Without a note it is unintelligible.

book_verdict: The transcription of this Keil page is close to exact, and the translation is faithful, with accurate, useful glosses on the metrical terms. The only weak spot is the rendered apparatus, where the sigla ς and 'Val.' are expanded on guesswork ('later manuscripts', 'Valerius').
